name.description: Cluster name. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, 3-31 characters, must start with a letter.

size.description: T-shirt size. The platform resolves it to a worker instance type and node count; a business unit never names an instance type directly. Changing what a size means is a sizing-map change and needs no manifest edits.

namespaces.description: Kubernetes namespaces to create on the cluster.

name.description: Bucket name. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, 3-41 characters, must start with a letter. Must be globally unique across AliCloud.

size.description: Storage tier. The platform resolves it to a concrete storage class; a business unit never names one directly.

versioning.description: Keep previous versions of overwritten or deleted objects.

prefixes.description: Key prefixes to create up front, for example "incoming/". These are also the only prefixes an access claim in the security lane may be scoped to.

name.description: Logical name for the grant. Becomes the RAM role, group and policy name; a business unit never names those objects directly.

identity_type.description: Who the grant is for. "workload" binds a Kubernetes service account through RRSA; "group" binds a directory group of human users.

level.description: Access level. The platform resolves it to a concrete action list held in the access map. A business unit cannot enumerate API actions, which is what keeps privilege escalation out of a claim.
